correctness.rationale: A uniform factorial tail bounds finite decreasing-priority ancestry for all positive rates, justifying both fixed-slow-time and terminal first-stage/second-stage coupling. For every k>=4, even start rods have precisely the conflict graph of unit length-r RSA on compressed indices. The empty-interval hierarchy gives saturated maximal-gap density exp(-2H_(r-1)). Geometry shows physical gaps are 2g (k even) or 2g+1 (k odd), with g<=r-1. Consequently only odd k admit a slow rod, and these maximal gaps are disjoint and fill independently with probability 1-exp(-s). Exact occupation per physical parity and the k^-1 asymptotic follow. Standalone seeded verifier passed 2138 supplementary checks; no infinite result is inferred from finite sampling.

originality.rationale: The asserted all-k parity classification, separate even/odd slow-time profiles and exact noncommuting weak-channel boundary are not shown by the inspected individual staggered dimer and trimer cases or by published uniform-RSA gap densities. Pinsky Theorems 1, 2 and 4 are acknowledged as strong inputs/related staged arguments; they do not assert the identical-length, start-parity rate limit. Novelty is provisional because the closely relevant 1994 article was accessible only as an abstract and comprehensive priority remains unverified.

value.rationale: The meaningful question is whether adding an arbitrarily weak adsorption channel changes final coverage after a jam. An unbounded family exhibits a new universal odd/even dichotomy: all even rod lengths have no delayed admissible footprint, whereas all odd lengths >=5 have exact positive maximal-hole response. The exact noncommutation, sublattice-resolved slow-time crossover, and decaying sharp jump with rod length offer physically interpretable structural information not supplied by finite examples or standard homogeneous parking constants.
